question: Do WebGL 2 / OpenGL ES normative sources require the exact R85 f32-staged arithmetic and bitwise Half result?

sourceLock.authority: Official conformance repository, non-normative implementation receipt

preregisteredChecks: all source downloads succeed and hashes are recorded
OpenGL ES general floating-point section says otherwise-unspecified representation and operation details are not specified
OpenGL ES acknowledges distinct implementations may differ pixel-for-pixel
blend computation precision floor is destination-component precision, not a mandated Float32 stage sequence
EXT_color_buffer_float adds floating-point color-buffer blending applicability but no precision or rounding rule
EXT_float_blend enables 32-bit floating-point blending but adds no precision or rounding rule
WebGL extension pages add no WebGL-specific behavioral precision rule
official WebGL conformance lineage uses a non-zero image threshold and is not reclassified as normative

decisionRule.specGuaranteed: Only if a normative source explicitly fixes complement/product/sum precision, rounding boundaries and Half storage rounding sufficiently to force the R85 bits.
decisionRule.empiricalOnly: If sources define equations and a minimum precision but leave operation details or implementation variation open.
decisionRule.noNovelty: If the audit cannot distinguish those cases, preserve R85 unchanged and record Unknown.

prohibitions: Do not render the R85 target again on SwiftShader.
Do not treat absence of a keyword as standalone proof; combine it with positive normative clauses.
Do not treat the conformance repository as a normative specification.
Do not modify production Mothers, Canonical Truth or Frozen R1.
